problem: On long-horizon mobile manipulation in the Home Assistant Benchmark (HAB), prior skill-chaining pipelines (TP+SRL from Habitat 2.0) chain stationary, fixed-base manipulation skills with a point-goal navigation skill. This setup suffers from hand-off errors: navigation often stops where the target is out of reach or infeasible for the stationary skill. As a result, success on the full HAB tasks is near zero.
motivation: Monolithic end-to-end RL fails on these long tasks because of sample complexity, reward design and exploration, so a modular approach is the practical route. It only works if subtasks are formulated so the skills compose. The authors observe that navigation is robust to its initial state but stationary manipulation has a tiny feasible initial set. They also note there are many valid base positions for manipulation, while the point-goal reward forces navigation to memorize a single, heuristically chosen one.
key_idea: Give the manipulation skills base mobility so their feasible initial-state set grows to cover navigation's terminal states, then reuse that enlarged set of initial base positions as a region goal (plus a collision penalty) when training the navigation skill.
insight:
Subtask formulation, meaning which initial states each skill is trained on, is the lever for composability; they frame it as a trade-off between achievability and composability.
- Mobile skills beat stationary ones: M+P 64.9/36.2 vs S+P 57.4/31.1 average SR (cross-config/cross-layout).
- Simply enlarging the initial states of stationary skills hurts: S(L)+P reaches only 37.7/18.1, and Pick success on TidyHouse drops from 95% to 45%.
- A collision penalty helps: S+P(C) 65.2/44.6 and M+P(C) 67.9/49.2.
- Removing goal ambiguity with the region goal adds more, especially across layouts: M3 71.2/55.0.
- Initial-state radius for mobile skills has a sweet spot:
  - 1.5m: 69.5/52.1
  - 2m: 71.2/55.0
  - 2.5m: 67.4/49.7
  - 4m: 55.2/38.9
  - random orientation: 67.5/46.4
- So mobile manipulation skills cannot absorb long-range navigation.
method: Task decomposition with a perfect task planner: each HAB task is a fixed sequence of parameterized skills (Navigate, Pick, Place, Open/Close drawer, Open/Close fridge). Each skill takes a 3D GeometricGoal position (the object's start s0 or goal s*). Skills are executed sequentially, and the arm is reset to its rest pose after each skill.

Mobile manipulation skills: the arm action space (7-DoF delta joint targets plus gripper) is augmented with 2-D base linear/angular velocity. This lets Pick/Place/Open/Close move the base to correct for imperfect navigation.

Unified initial-state generation: the floor is discretized at 5×5 cm² and navigable cells are kept. Candidates are cells within 2m of the target (Pick/Place) or within a container-relative region (Open/Close). A position is sampled with noise and rejection; the low rejection rate allows on-the-fly sampling during training. The base faces the target.

Region-goal navigation reward: r = -Δgeo to the region {g} + λ_succ·1[d_geo({g})≤D ∧ d_ang≤Θ] - r_col - r_slack. Geodesic distance to the region is the minimum over grid cells in the manipulation candidate set. The angular-shaping term of the point-goal reward is dropped, and a collision-force penalty min(0.001·C_t, 0.2) is added.

Skill policies: a 3-layer CNN encodes head and arm depth (128×128); features are concatenated with proprioception, goal positions and the previous action, then fed to a 1-layer GRU. Each skill is trained with PPO for 100M steps with 64 parallel environments and 3 seeds. Skills are trained per task to avoid ambiguity; navigation uses a discrete action set of 4 linear × 5 angular velocities, with stop.

Proprioceptive termination at chaining time: Pick/Place end when the end-effector is within 15cm of the rest position with the right holding state. Open/Close use a displacement heuristic. Navigate ends on its stop action. Every skill also has a step cap of 200 (manipulation) or 500 (navigation).

setting.backbone: Per-skill PPO policies: 3-layer CNN (depth) + 1-layer GRU + linear heads, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: RL in simulation per task: 6400 generated episodes over 64 ReplicaCAD scenes (4 macro variations), 100M environment steps per skill, 3 seeds per skill; no extra data
setting.observation: head + arm depth (128×128), arm joint positions, end-effector position, holding flag, goal position in base/EE frames via perfect GPS+Compass (navigation: head depth + goal in base frame only)
setting.action_space: manipulation skills: 10-dim continuous (2-D base velocity, 7-D delta joint targets, 1-D gripper with abstract snap grasp within 15cm); navigation: discrete (4 linear × 5 angular velocity choices incl. stop) converted to continuous base velocity
setting.privileged: perfect task planner (given subtask sequence); GeometricGoal 3D start/goal positions of target objects; perfect GPS+Compass; abstract (snap) grasp; arm reset by directly setting PD joint targets

numbers.bench: other:HAB (Home Assistant Benchmark: avg of TidyHouse, PrepareGroceries, SetTable)
numbers.extra: Cross-configuration setting: 100 episodes per task from 20 held-out scenes of the 4 training macro variations (unseen object/goal configurations). SR is the full-task success averaged over 3 tasks and over 9 runs (3 training seeds × 3 init seeds). Perfect task planner; abstract grasp; SetTable modified (fruit placed on table rather than in bowl).
numbers.evidence: Sec 5.3: "Our method M3 achieves an average success rate of 71.2% in the cross-configuration setting, and 55.0% in the cross-layout setting, over all 3 tasks."

numbers.bench: other:HAB (Home Assistant Benchmark: avg of TidyHouse, PrepareGroceries, SetTable)
numbers.extra: Cross-layout setting: 100 episodes per task from the held-out ReplicaCAD macro variation (unseen furniture layout). SR is averaged over 3 tasks and 9 runs. Perfect task planner; abstract grasp; SetTable modified.
numbers.evidence: Sec 5.3: "Our method M3 achieves an average success rate of 71.2% in the cross-configuration setting, and 55.0% in the cross-layout setting, over all 3 tasks."

numbers_note: Per-task progressive completion rates (TidyHouse, PrepareGroceries, SetTable) are given only in figures (Fig. 3, Fig. 5, appendix figure). The text reports only success averaged over the 3 tasks. The intro rounds the combined average to "63%" vs "50%" for the best baseline. HAB here uses the authors' own episode generation (ReplicaCAD v1.4), not an official challenge split. Mapping cross-configuration to val-seen and cross-layout to val-unseen is my interpretation.
results:
M3 reaches an average full-task success of 71.2% (cross-configuration) and 55.0% (cross-layout) over the 3 HAB tasks. It beats:
- monolithic RL (1.8%/1.8%)
- the authors' improved reimplementation of Habitat 2.0 TP+SRL, S+P (57.4%/31.1%)
- M+P (64.9%/36.2%)

The original TP+SRL success rates are reported as near zero. Gains are largest in the cross-layout setting (+18.8 over M+P).
limitations: Simulation only, with abstract snap grasp: the SetTable objective had to be weakened because stable placement into a bowl is not controllable. The authors leave fully dynamic simulation and real-robot deployment to future work.
Relies on privileged structure: a perfect task planner, known 3D start/goal positions, perfect GPS+Compass, and skills trained separately per task.
Mobile manipulation skills cannot handle long-range navigation: with a 4m initial radius, SR drops to 55.2/38.9, so a separate navigation skill is still required.
